review_notes: I read the whole theorem. I grepped for the local `have`s to get line numbers and read `pushPt_act_natCast_eq_nsmulPt`, which is the existing API the `nX` blocks call. I did not read the full definitions of `FakeEllipticCurve.IsLevelIsogeny`, `mapPt` or `nsmulPt`. The exact form of `h11`/`h12` (the composite `φ ≫ ψ = act (z ℓ)`) is therefore inferred from how `comp_eq` and `pushPt_act_natCast_eq_nsmulPt` are applied. The proposed lemma signature would need adjusting to the real types. The two findings are the only repeated nontrivial blocks. `hk12`/`hk21` are one-line symmetric terms and do not qualify, and `comp_eq` is already a shared lemma.

findings.excerpt: rw [comp_eq φ1 hφ1 ψ1 hψ1 _ (u.1.act_over _) h11 t P]; exact CerednikDrinfeld.QM.FakeEllipticCurve.pushPt_act_natCast_eq_nsmulPt u.1 hΛ.one_mem ℓ hℓΛ t P
findings.problem: Four statements share one argument: for an isogeny pair φ : E → E' and ψ : E' → E whose composite is the scalar action of ℓ on E, pushing a point forward along φ then ψ equals `nsmulPt E.L t ℓ`. Each copy restates the long ∀-statement and repeats the same two-step proof, a `comp_eq` rewrite followed by `pushPt_act_natCast_eq_nsmulPt`. Only the curve (u.1, d, u.1, d') and the isogeny data (φ1/ψ1, ψ1/φ1, φ2/ψ2, ψ2/φ2) change. n11 and n21 differ only in index, and n12 and n22 likewise.
findings.proposed_change: Add one private lemma, or a local `have` generalised over the curve and maps. Roughly: `∀ {E E' : FakeEllipticCurve Λ N k} (φ ψ) (hφ hψ) (hcomp : φ ≫ ψ = E.act (z ℓ)) {T} (t) (P : SchemeHomOver t E.f), mapPt ψ hψ (mapPt φ hφ P) = nsmulPt E.L t ℓ P`. The proof is `rw [comp_eq φ hφ ψ hψ _ (E.act_over _) hcomp t P]; exact pushPt_act_natCast_eq_nsmulPt E hΛ.one_mem ℓ hℓΛ t P`. Then n11 := lemma φ1 ψ1 .. h11, n12 := lemma ψ1 φ1 .. h12, n21 := lemma φ2 ψ2 .. h21, n22 := lemma ψ2 φ2 .. h22. Each is a one-line instantiation under the same hypotheses (`hΛ.one_mem`, `hℓΛ`), so no new imports are needed.
findings.benefit: The argument is written once and the four uses are short instances. The reader sees that all four are the same fact with the roles swapped. A change to the `comp_eq`/`pushPt_act_natCast_eq_nsmulPt` interface is made in one place instead of four.

findings.problem: onto1 and onto2 are the same lifting statement and the same call, including the repeated disjointness lambda `fun t P h hC => u.2.levK_disjoint t P ((hkerᵢ t P).1 h) hC`. They differ only in target curve d/d' and the index 1/2. The long ∀-statements are written twice.
findings.proposed_change: Make a local `have onto : ∀ (e : FakeEllipticCurve Λ N k) (φ) (hφ) (hmul) (hker) (hlev), ∀ {T} t (Q : SchemeHomOver t e.f), FactorsThrough e.lev Q → ∃ P, FactorsThrough u.1.lev P ∧ mapPt φ hφ P = Q`. Its proof is the `exists_factorsThrough_lev_mapPt_eq_of_forall_eq_one` call with the disjointness lambda built from `hker`. Then onto1 and onto2 are instantiations. It could be folded into the shared lemma for n11–n22, which would take the full isogeny data as a bundle. The lemma `exists_factorsThrough_lev_mapPt_eq_of_forall_eq_one` could also directly take the kernel-iff hypothesis `hker` instead of the derived lambda, so the callers pass `hker` unchanged.
findings.benefit: This removes the duplicated statement and disjointness plumbing, and makes the symmetry between the two isogenies explicit. It also shortens the main proof, which is currently a long sequence of near-identical haves.
